title: Lens Optics Demo
prompt:
Create an interactive thin lens optics demonstration using Three.js. The scene should visualize a converging (convex) lens with an object, and show the resulting image formation based on the thin lens equation (1/f = 1/do + 1/di).

SCENE SETUP:
- Use an orthographic or perspective camera looking down the Y-axis (top-down 2D view) so the optical axis runs along the X-axis.
- Background color: #1a1a2e (dark blue). Add a grid helper on the XZ plane for reference.
- Draw the principal (optical) axis as a horizontal white dashed line along Z=0, X from -15 to 15.
- Place a thin lens at the origin (X=0) represented by a vertical blue line or double-arrow shape (height ~4 units). Label it 'Lens'.
- Mark two focal points as small yellow spheres at X = -focalLength and X = +focalLength on the axis. Default focal length = 3 units.
- Place an 'object' (a red vertical arrow pointing up, height 2 units) at X = -6 (left side of lens). The arrow base sits on the optical axis.
- Calculate the image position using 1/f = 1/do + 1/di where do = distance from object to lens (positive). Compute di and magnification m = -di/do. Place a green vertical arrow at X = +di with height = |m| * objectHeight. If m < 0, the arrow points downward (inverted image). If di is negative, place the image on the same side as the object (virtual image) and make it semi-transparent.
- Draw three principal rays from the tip of the object arrow through the lens to the image tip:
  1. A ray parallel to the axis that refracts through the far focal point.
  2. A ray through the center of the lens that continues straight.
  3. A ray through the near focal point that refracts parallel to the axis.
  Use yellow lines for these rays.

USER INTERACTIONS:
- The object arrow can be dragged left/right along the optical axis (constrain X between -12 and -1). Update image position and rays in real-time as the object moves.
- Add a DOM slider (id='focalLengthSlider') ranging from 1 to 6 (step 0.5) to adjust the focal length. Default value 3. Update focal point positions, image, and rays when changed.
- Add a button (id='toggleLensType') that toggles between converging (convex, f > 0) and diverging (concave, f < 0) lens. When diverging, focal length becomes negative, the lens visual changes to a concave shape or different color (e.g., orange), and image formation updates accordingly (diverging lens always produces virtual upright image for real objects).
- Add a HUD div (id='infoPanel') showing: Object Distance (do), Image Distance (di), Magnification (m), and Image Type ('Real/Inverted' or 'Virtual/Upright').

STATE MANAGEMENT:
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- objectDistance: (positive number, distance from object to lens)
- imageDistance: (number, positive = real image on far side, negative = virtual image on same side)
- magnification: (number, negative = inverted)
- focalLength: (number, positive for converging, negative for diverging)
- lensType: 'converging' or 'diverging'
- imageType: 'real' or 'virtual'
- objectX: X position of the object (negative number)
- imageX: X position of the image

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame or on interaction.

ASSETS: None needed, build all geometry procedurally.
physics_constraints: Thin lens equation: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di. Magnification: m = -di/do. For converging lens (f>0) with object beyond focal point, image is real and inverted. With object inside focal point, image is virtual and upright. For diverging lens (f<0), image is always virtual and upright for real objects.
